name: Cliniko vs SimplePractice
title: Cliniko vs SimplePractice: Practice Management Comparison for Allied Health & Mental Health
description: Compare Cliniko and SimplePractice - two popular practice management platforms. See differences in pricing, features, telehealth, and target audiences.

summary.bottom_line: Cliniko and SimplePractice serve different primary markets. Cliniko is an allied health-focused platform popular globally (especially Australia/UK) with flat pricing and no feature tiers, while SimplePractice is a US-focused mental health EHR with comprehensive billing and e-prescribing. Choose Cliniko for allied health practices wanting simple pricing; choose SimplePractice for US mental health practices needing insurance billing and e-prescribing.

sections.heading: Cliniko vs SimplePractice: Overview
sections.content: Cliniko and SimplePractice are both cloud-based practice management platforms, but they serve different primary markets. Cliniko was built in Australia for allied health practitioners (physiotherapists, chiropractors, osteopaths, psychologists) and is popular globally. SimplePractice was built in the US primarily for mental health professionals (therapists, counselors, psychologists) with a focus on US insurance billing workflows. Both offer scheduling, notes, and patient management, but differ significantly in their approach to pricing, billing, and telehealth.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Cliniko uses a unique flat-pricing model where all features are included at every tier—pricing only scales by number of practitioners ($45/month solo to $395/month for 26-200 practitioners). Prices haven't changed since 2011. SimplePractice uses feature-tiered pricing: Starter ($49/mo) has basic features, Essential ($79/mo) adds telehealth and billing, and Plus ($99/mo) includes all features. SimplePractice also has paid add-ons for AI notes ($35/mo) and e-prescribing ($49/mo).

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: The biggest differences are in telehealth and US insurance billing. SimplePractice includes built-in HIPAA-compliant telehealth and robust US insurance claims submission with clearinghouse integration. Cliniko does not include native telehealth and has limited US insurance billing support (better for international markets). SimplePractice offers e-prescribing for prescribers; Cliniko does not. Cliniko's strength is its simplicity and consistent feature set regardless of pricing tier.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your location, specialty, and billing needs:

recommendations.when: You're an allied health practice (physio, chiro, massage), based outside the US (especially Australia/UK), want all features without upsells, or prefer simple flat-rate pricing
You're a US-based mental health professional, need insurance billing, want built-in telehealth, or require e-prescribing capabilities
You're a psychologist in private practice with primarily self-pay clients and minimal insurance billing needs

faqs.q: Is Cliniko good for mental health practices?
faqs.a: Cliniko can work for mental health practices, especially those with self-pay clients outside the US. However, it lacks mental health-specific features like e-prescribing, US insurance billing, and built-in telehealth that SimplePractice offers.

No, Cliniko does not include native telehealth. You would need to use a separate telehealth platform like Doxy.me or Zoom. SimplePractice includes built-in HIPAA-compliant telehealth on Essential and Plus plans.

faqs.q: Which is cheaper: Cliniko or SimplePractice?
faqs.a: For solo practitioners, they're similar: Cliniko is $45/month with all features, SimplePractice Starter is $49/month with basic features. However, SimplePractice Essential ($79/mo) is needed for telehealth and billing. Cliniko's flat pricing means no surprise upsells.

faqs.q: Can I switch from SimplePractice to Cliniko?
faqs.a: Yes, Cliniko offers free data migration from other practice management systems. Contact their support for import assistance. Consider whether you'll lose US insurance billing capabilities you may need.
